source.title: Transferable Perturbations of Deep Feature Distributions
source.authors: Nathan Inkawhich; Kevin J Liang; L. Carin; Yi-Ran Chen

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites convergent learning and discusses task/data-specific versus model-specific features, but its experiments test adversarial attack transfer—not whether independently trained models’ representations become more similar.
record.gate_note: No results measure inter-model representation similarity or its change with model scale or capability. The reported attack-transfer rates and feature disruptions are related findings, but do not test any listed claim version; the attack results below are recorded as versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study develops a feature-distribution adversarial attack and reports targeted and untargeted transfer rates between three pre-trained ImageNet CNNs (DN121, RN50, VGG19). It never measures representational similarity, alignment, mapping quality or shared features between models. It invokes convergent learning (Li et al. 2016) only as an interpretation: intermediate layers hold task/data-specific features and later layers model-specific ones. Attack transfer and cross-model 'disruption' (Fig. 3, measured with each model's own auxiliary classifiers) are related but different constructs, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim state-of-the-art targeted blackbox transfer. They find source layer depth strongly affects transferability, possibly reflecting a task/data-specific to model-specific transition. Optimal layers are class-separable but not overly correlated with the whitebox output. Transferable attacks strongly disrupt blackbox intermediate features.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates adversarial attacks; it does not apply the original studies’ representation-similarity methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack transfer varies with the source model and feature layer; attack success also varies by attack variant and perturbation strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Targeted feature-distribution attacks from intermediate layers transfer across ImageNet CNN architectures (tSuc 15.9–30.9% at eps 16/255) much better than logit-layer attacks. The optimal source layer is the same regardless of the target model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intermediate-layer features of different ImageNet CNNs are shared enough that perturbing them transfers adversarial effects across architectures, while last-layer features are model-specific.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal-layer FDA+fd attacks cause high disruption of target-class probability throughout blackbox models' layers (about 80% max from DN121/RN50 whiteboxes, about 40% from VGG19). The values are shown in a figure only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbations of mid-depth features in one CNN induce corresponding class-feature shifts in other CNNs' intermediate layers.

record.problems: Only three pre-trained ImageNet CNN architectures are evaluated; the results concern adversarial transfer rather than direct representational alignment. Some layer-wise analyses are presented in figures without numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted as rows because they report attack comparisons, layer-wise disruption, auxiliary-model correlation, or class separability rather than a listed representation-convergence version.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no cross-model alignment measure.
No vision-language or paired image-caption data.
No models from different seeds; all three are different architectures.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test between models.
No comparison of interpretable features or circuits across models.
No comparison of similarity metrics or input distributions.
No measure of how complete alignment is, and no attribution to data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Li et al. 2016 (an original source) as a theory its interpretation extends, but it collects no representation-similarity evidence. The relation 'discusses' and tranche T6 are kept.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling or capability sweep and no measurement of representational alignment across independently trained models.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language models.
No comparison across random initializations or measurement of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No comparison of representation-similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
No test of whether representational alignment is incomplete or explained by shared data or objectives.

relation.reason: Section 6 connects its proposed task/data-specific to model-specific transition to convergent learning, without measuring convergence between models.

tranche.reason: The study measures adversarial attack transfer, feature disruption, within-model output correlation and class separability; these do not test any listed convergence version.

source_check.notes: The eight values correctly report the study's own attack performance and should not serve as convergence evidence. Section 5.2 averages results over four random 10k splits and reports standard deviations below 1%.
